cf.title: Fix pg_basebackup long-path test on Windows

input.subject: [PATCH v1] Fix pg_basebackup long-path test on Windows

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated with a reproducible case in message #1: a 253-character path, an unchecked mkdir, and a misleading later error. The fix changes one TAP test file and has no user-visible surface. Confidence is medium because the code was not read and the v3 diff is not shown.

brief.title: Fix pg_basebackup TAP test long-path mkdir failure on Windows
brief.problem: On Windows, the pg_basebackup TAP test creates $superlongname through the build-tree side of a junction, so the path can exceed the 248-character directory limit. Perl's mkdir then fails without a check, and the test later fails with a misleading CREATE TABLESPACE "directory does not exist" error. This affects developers and buildfarm members running the tests on Windows.
brief.proposed_design: The patch creates the long-named tablespace directory through the short system temporary directory side of the junction. It also checks the result of mkdir and calls BAIL_OUT with the `$!` variable. on failure, so a setup failure is reported where it happens. Only src/bin/pg_basebackup/t/010_pg_basebackup.pl changes.
author_claims: The unpatched test fails and the patched test passes all 149 subtests on native ARM64 and on an x64 cross-build, Windows 11, MSVC 19.44.
v3, rebased on 8e82d6610e7, passes all 151 subtests on native ARM64 and x64 under ARM64 emulation, with directory-cleanup warnings.
A GitHub-hosted Windows x64 build passes all 152 pg_basebackup subtests, with "all three patches" applied.
No earlier proposal covers this unchecked long-directory creation; a 2023 thread covered a related long-file test.
brief.thread_state: Daniel Gustafsson asked for the `$!` variable. in the BAIL_OUT message, and v2 added it. The author posted v3 as a rebase and asked for another look, but nobody has replied yet.
unclear: The material does not say whether the test fails on the buildfarm or CI today, or only on some build paths.
The directory-cleanup warnings in the v3 runs are not explained, and the material does not say whether the patch causes them.
"All three patches" in message #4 is not explained, since only one patch is attached.
The material does not say whether the fix should be back-patched to stable branches.
The v3 commit message and its diff against v2 are not shown.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry is tagged Bugfix for a test in 010_pg_basebackup.pl, and the thread does not say which stable branches need it.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Does the test fail on any buildfarm member or on CI today, or only when the build-tree path is long enough to pass 248 characters?
Do the directory-cleanup warnings in the v3 runs also appear without the patch, or does creating the directory through the short side of the junction cause them?
Should the fix be back-patched, and if so, to which stable branches does the same unchecked mkdir apply?
What are the "three patches" applied in the GitHub-hosted Windows x64 run, given that the thread attaches only one?
Does the test still exercise a long tablespace path after the directory is created through the short system temporary directory?

committability.owner_note: Daniel Gustafsson commented on v1 in message #2, and the demand review note describes him as a committer. Nobody has replied to v3 yet. The owner needs to know the TAP test framework and Windows path handling.
committability.liability: One TAP test file. The owner signs for the test passing on Windows buildfarm members and for any cleanup warnings the new directory location may cause. The liability is small and limited to the test suite.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 in response to review and rebased to v3 with new test runs, which suggests continued follow-up.

priority.reason: The patch is about 1.5 KB in one test file and helps developers and buildfarm members who run the suite on Windows with long build paths. It adds no runtime code and makes a setup failure report at its source.

provisional_note: The code and the v3 diff were not read. Two things could not be checked: whether the cleanup warnings come from this change, and whether the test still covers a long tablespace path.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_basebackup: add test about zstd compress option
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a test to pg_basebackup's TAP tests that exercises the zstd compression option, later extended to verify the generated files with the zstd binary. A follow-up version refactored the test to cover multiple compression methods (gzip, lz4, zstd) and check output with each respective decompression program.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas pointed out that existing tests in src/bin/pg_verifybackup (008_untar.pl and 009_extract.pl) already cover compressed base backups, and that the only additional scenario the new test could catch was not worth the extra CPU cycles. Ian Lawrence Barwick and the author agreed the test did not add anything, and the entry was closed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I would be inclined to dismiss that particular scenario as not important
enough to be worth the additional CPU cycles.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent pg_basebackup running as root
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make pg_basebackup refuse to run as root (except for --help/--version), matching the existing checks in initdb, pg_ctl and pg_upgrade, so it cannot create root-owned files in a data directory that the postmaster could not use. The change was not to be backpatched, as it alters behavior.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was committed by Michael Paquier and then reverted after a separate discussion that is linked but not included in the visible messages. The visible messages do not show why.

precedents_retrieved.title: Application name for pg_basebackup, pg_receivewal and pg_recvlogical
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an -a / --appname command line switch to pg_basebackup, pg_receivewal and pg_recvlogical to set the application name of their connection. The stated use case was letting pg_receivewal connect as a synchronous client listed in synchronous_standby_names.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers noted that the application name can already be set through the environment variable or the application_name parameter in the connection string passed with -d, so a new switch was not needed. The patch was marked rejected in the CommitFest app on that basis, and the author agreed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I don't think we need a new comand line switch for it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Windows pg_basebackup unable to create >2GB pg_wal.tar tarballs ("could not close file: Invalid argument" when creating pg_wal.tar of size ~ 2^31 bytes)
precedents_retrieved.summary: On Windows, pg_basebackup in tar mode fails with "could not close file: Invalid argument" when pg_wal.tar grows past 2^31 bytes, because off_t, lseek() and ftruncate() are 32-bit there. A proof-of-concept patch redirects lseek() to _lseeki64() so the WAL tar file can exceed 2 GiB.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last message discusses how to back-patch the fix, including an ftruncate() replacement, and nobody objects to it. The entry was withdrawn three days later, and no message gives a reason.

precedents_retrieved.title: Move tablespace path re-creation from the makefiles to pg_regress (test for mkdir function in the backend)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a mkdir() SQL function to regress.c, so the backend creates the test tablespace directory instead of pg_regress. It aims to restore installcheck runs where the server user differs from the pg_regress user, which commit 6c788d9 broke.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it because nobody showed a need to act: Christoph Berg had a workaround for the Debian suite, and it was unclear whether a server user different from the pg_regress user should be supported at all. Noah Misch also reported that the patch fails when make check is followed by make installcheck against a server running as another user, because rmtree() cannot remove the server-created directory.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
At the
same time, Christoph has a workaround for the Debian suite, so it does
not seem like there is anything to do now, anyway.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_basebackup to adjust existing data directory permissions
precedents_retrieved.summary: pg_basebackup was proposed to change the permissions of an existing target data directory to the required permissions, as initdb does, so that the postmaster can start on the resulting backup. The discussion later extended this to a -g {inherit|none|group} option controlling group access on the backup, including changes to BASE_BACKUP so that tar-mode backups carry the chosen permissions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers did not agree on the desired behavior. Peter Eisentraut and David Steele considered the proposed options too complicated for a problem the user can fix by changing permissions, while others wanted the current behavior changed; the author's tally showed support and opposition. Alvaro Herrera noted the discussion was inconclusive and the patch dormant, and after a further idle period the entry was closed as returned with little useful feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There's been at lot of
discussion but it doesn't seem conclusive; it doesn't look like we know
what we actually want to do.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Remove reset of testtablespace from pg_regress on Windows"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Remove reset of testtablespace from pg_regress on Windows"
Reverted commit(s): Remove reset of testtablespace from pg_regress on Windows; Lower privilege level of programs calling regression_main
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 2b2a070, that moved the reset of path
"testtablespace" used by the regression tests as a path for tablespaces
(via --outputdir) from pg_regress to the MSVC script vcregress.pl, as
this broke the behavior added by ce5d342 to be able to safely run the
regression test suite with an administrative Windows account using a
restricted token.

Note that before 2b2a070, the code doing the reset in pg_regress.c
included a comment telling that we had better move that out to a
different place, leading to the mistake done in 2b2a070.  Fix this
comment, and document instead that we had better never remove this code,
for the sake of not breaking again the behavior we expect on Windows.

Thanks to Thomas Munro and Andrew Dunstan for the discussion.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add tablespace tap test to pg_rewind
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a TAP test for pg_rewind that checks tablespaces created before and after standby promotion, modeled on 002_databases.pl. It extends RewindTest.pm, PostgresNode.pm and RecursiveCopy.pm so a standby can be built with tablespace mapping and symlinks can be copied.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The test setup made the primary, the backup and the standbys share the same tablespace paths, so multiple standbys from one backup would use one tablespace directory and the source and target servers would overwrite each other. A correct test needs a tablespace mapping option for the file-level backup routines in RecursiveCopy.pm and PostgresNode::init_from_backup, and an option in pg_rewind similar to pg_basebackup's --tablespace-mapping. Michael Paquier judged this a large amount of work that may be hard to justify.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
And on top of that there is of course the argument of pg_rewind which
would need an option similar to pg_basebackup's --tablespace-mapping
so as a target instance does not finish by using the same tablespace
path as the source where there is a tablespace of difference during
the operation.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums"
Reverted commit(s): Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 2aa6e33, that added a fast path to skip
anti-wraparound and non-aggressive autovacuum jobs (these have no sense
as anti-wraparound implies aggressive).  With a cluster using a high
amount of relations with a portion of them being heavily updated, this
could cause autovacuum to lock down, with autovacuum workers attempting
repeatedly those jobs on the same relations for the same database, that
just kept being skipped.  This lock down can be solved with a manual
VACUUM FREEZE.

Justin King has reported one environment where the issue happened, and
Julien Rouhaud and I have been able to reproduce it in a second
environment.  With a very aggressive autovacuum_freeze_max_age,
triggering those jobs with pgbench is a matter of minutes, and hitting
the lock down is a lot harder (my local tests failed to do that).

Note that anti-wraparound and non-aggressive jobs can only be triggered
on a subset of shared catalogs:
- pg_auth_members
- pg_authid
- pg_database
- pg_replication_origin
- pg_shseclabel
- pg_subscription
- pg_tablespace
While the lock down was possible down to v12, the root cause of those
jobs is a much older issue, which needs more analysis.

Bonus thanks to Andres Freund for the discussion.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found, and the corpus search returned no related rejected attempt. Message #1 points to a 2023 discussion of a related pg_basebackup long-file test, but the thread does not report it as a rejection of this fix, so no earlier objection applies.

The patch changes only one TAP test file and has no user-facing surface: no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog, pg_dump output, psql behaviour or client-visible change, so the standards and compatibility angle finds nothing to object to. Whether the test still covers long tablespace paths when the directory is created through the short side of the junction is a test-coverage question for another angle.

The patch changes only one TAP test script, src/bin/pg_basebackup/t/010_pg_basebackup.pl. It does not touch on-disk format, WAL, replication, catalogs, the wire protocol or the extension ABI, so this angle has nothing to object to.

The patch changes only a TAP test script, 010_pg_basebackup.pl, and makes no change to server, client, privileges, authentication or anything a user can reach. The temporary directory and junction already exist in the test, so the security angle has nothing to object to.

The patch changes one TAP test file, adds no runtime code, no API and no hot-path cost, and the mkdir check makes future setup failures loud. A committer may ask whether the directory-cleanup warnings seen in the v3 runs come from this change, but that is a question for review, not an objection.

This is a test-only fix in 010_pg_basebackup.pl, and I know of no existing feature, extension or tool that already solves it. The patch reuses the short-path junction that the test already creates, so it adds no second mechanism and leaves nothing for an extension or hook to do.

This is a test-only fix for a reproducible failure on Windows builds, and it costs nothing outside one TAP file. Demand is not the right test here. Developers and buildfarm members who run the suite on Windows need a test that passes or fails where the real error is, and a committer reviewed it in message #2.
